svg.text: 62 bytes at $FF8A00: sixteen halftone words, eleven pointer registers, three end masks, and one byte of control.
the map, with the decode's own strobes beside it
all ones · halftone · source · S AND H
the last four bytes — one word's worth of control, and the only place a model can go wrong
BUSY is a read bit and a start bit at once: write 1 and it starts, write 0 and it pauses, and it reads 1 through the pause.
The interrupt line is a duplicate of BUSY, so completion is a falling edge — never a pulse. FXSR and NFSR change how many source reads a line spends.
why the halftone block is first
sixteen word selects at 2-byte steps, $00–$1E, is 32 bytes — the pattern, exactly
why the rest is not word-aligned
HOP, OP, LINE·SMUDGE·HOG·BUSY and SKEW·FXSR·NFSR are bytes inside one word
Provenance: the register map and every quoted field from Atari's BLiTTER manual; the strobe names (XSEL00…XSEL1E, XOPW, XHOPW, XSKEWW,
XLINEW, XSMUDGE, XFXSR, XRAMR/XRAMW) from sheet 9 of ST-4051, "Address decode and regs".
